channel.description: Recent content in Visual Studio on Sujith Quintelier

item.title: visualstudio: Preparing for Your Next Certification Could Start with Your Visual Studio Subscription
item.description:
The post says Visual Studio subscription holders may already have access to resources that can help prepare for Microsoft certification, including courses, labs, and hands-on exercises. It frames the subscription as a starting point for finding study materials and planning certification prep.

  • Source: Visual Studio Blog

item.title: visualstudio: Visual Studio October Update – Compare Commits to Your Code, Resolve Conflicts in Bulk, Keep Coding
item.description:
Visual Studio October update adds commit-to-working-tree comparison, bulk merge conflict resolution, and several editor/UX refinements. It also refreshes Copilot chat, Hot Exit, keyboard tab controls, and Fonts and Colors.

  • Source: Visual Studio Blog

item.title: visualstudio: Keep your investigation between sessions
item.description:
Visual Studio adds a standalone Markdown note for investigations and an opt-in Hot Exit preview that restores unsaved work in the next session. The post focuses on preserving work between sessions.

  • Source: Visual Studio Blog

item.title: github: GitHub Copilot in Visual Studio — September update
item.description:
GitHub’s September 2026 Visual Studio Copilot update adds pull request exploration in chat, support for choosing the AI model your team uses, and package vulnerability fixes surfaced directly from Visual Studio.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: visualstudio: Are You Getting Everything You Can from Your Visual Studio Subscription?
item.description:
The post reminds Visual Studio subscribers that their subscription may already include benefits they can use to try Azure services, access certification learning resources, and reuse UI/dashboard components. It is framed as a prompt to explore subscription perks they may be overlooking.

  • Source: Visual Studio Blog

item.title: visualstudio: Compare today’s code with an earlier commit
item.description:
Visual Studio now lets you compare your current working tree with an earlier commit without checking out that commit or switching branches. The feature is described in a Visual Studio Blog post about comparing historical code against today’s code.

  • Source: Visual Studio Blog

item.title: visualstudio: Organize and revisit tabs with the keyboard
item.description:
Visual Studio adds keyboard shortcuts to reorder document tabs and navigate back to them by their visual position. The update focuses on tab organization and quick revisiting without using the mouse.

  • Source: Visual Studio Blog

item.title: visualstudio: Stop waiting on a failed build
item.description:
Visual Studio now stops solution builds after the first project failure, so you can return to fixing the error sooner. The change reduces time spent waiting for the rest of the build to finish after an error has already occurred.

  • Source: Visual Studio Blog

item.title: visualstudio: New Tools, New Workflows and the Value of the Visual Studio Subscription: What We Learned at VSLive! San Diego
item.description:
At VSLive! San Diego, Microsoft discussed how developers are changing their coding workflows and learning new skills with Visual Studio and related tools. The post also highlights the value of a Visual Studio Subscription for expanding access to development resources.

  • Source: Visual Studio Blog

item.title: visualstudio: What Would You Build in Azure If You Didn’t Have to Ask for a Budget First?
item.description:
The post says eligible Visual Studio subscribers may already have access to a personal Azure sandbox, making it easier to try .NET apps, serverless, containers, proofs of concept, or unfamiliar Azure services without requesting a budget first.

  • Source: Visual Studio Blog

item.title: github: GitHub Copilot in Visual Studio — August update
item.description:
GitHub Copilot in Visual Studio’s August 2026 update adds more control over Copilot reasoning, model selection, sharing specialized agents within teams, and timing code review requests. The post is a high-level changelog summary rather than a detailed feature list.

  • Source: GitHub
